what: the metaphor-free guard's tests do not use the spec-binding describe convention the scenario bridge expects, so the scenario verifier reports all of the node's scenarios unbound even though each has a test; a judge has to re-derive the coverage by hand.

the guard excludes the plugin project spec's ledger by its one project folder name rather than by a rule covering every project under the plural specs tree, so a second project spec added there would have its ledger scanned.

the guard's allow-list still sanctions outward-caller references that name the consuming fleet layer's personas inside the CLI's unit lifecycle spec. The ratified rule for this change - a dependency must not name its consumer's personas - reads as retiring those too, but the allow-list was a separately ratified decision and this change left it in place for the owner to decide.
the plugin spec's inbox node is behavioral but has no What, Control Flow or Scenario map section, which the spec-gate conformance read flags as a warning.
